To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
miRNAs regulate lipid metabolism-related genes in enterocytes.
intestinal miRNas regulate lipid metabolism-related genes in enterocytes.

1) Intestinal lipid metabolism-related genes are regulated by miRNAs; 2) Intestinal miRNAs contribute in intestinal epithelial differentiation and 3) MiRNAs miR-31-3p, miR 99b-5, miR- 200a-5, mi-200b- 5 and miR- 425-5p regulate lipid metabolism-related genes in enterocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the intestinal miRNA-regulation of lipid metabolism-related genes and provides new insights into intestinal miRNA functions
a novel role for miRNAs as post-transcriptional regulators of intestinal lipid metabolism.
a novel approach to identify miRNAs that modulate lipid metabolism genes and their potential use as novel therapeutic targets in lipid metabolic disorders.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intestinal epithelium is a key regulator of lipid absorption and transport and that the intestinal epithelial miRNAs contribute in a major way to this function.
miRNAs are important regulators of lipid metabolism-related genes in intestinal cells and that miR-31- 5p and mi-99b- 5p may have therapeutic potential in intestinal lipid metabolism.
miRNAs play a role in lipid metabolism in enterocytes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intestinal miRNas play a role in lipid metabolism and epithelial differentiation.
intestinal miRNas regulate lipid metabolism in the enterocytes and that miR-31-4p, miR99b-5, miR-425, miR-31, miR-100b and miR-200 regulate the expression of HMGCS2, Acat-1 and OLR1.
miRNAs regulate lipid metabolism-related genes in enterocytes, and that miRNAs are potential therapeutic targets for lipid metabolism-associated pathophysiology.
The main takeaway from our work is that
miRNAs are important in regulating the expression of genes that control cholesterol and lipoproteins metabolism.
miRNAs play important roles in intestinal lipid metabolism.

miRNAs play a crucial role in lipid metabolism in the intestinal mucosal layer and that miR-31-4p, miR99b-5, miR-31p, miR200b-5 and miR-424-5p are the main regulators of lipid metabolism-related genes in enterocytes.
